definition: The Drug Abuse Screening Test is a questionnaire used to screen for drug-related problems and gauge how severe a person’s drug use may be. In the source packet, the DAST-20 is described as a widely used 20-item version that was adapted into Tagalog and shown to have acceptable reliability and validity.

reasons: The definition claims the Drug Abuse Screening Test is “a questionnaire”; the packet only describes it as a “drug-abuse screening tool” and does not explicitly state that it is a questionnaire.

The definition states it is used to “gauge how severe a person’s drug use may be.” The packet mentions an “urgent requirement” to understand “the severity of their drug use,” but it does not directly connect that function to DAST-20 as an explicit purpose in the way the definition claims.

While the packet supports that Tagalog versions of DAST-20 were “confirmed to be reliable and valid,” it does not support the broader framing that the overall Drug Abuse Screening Test (as a general term) is “widely used” and operates specifically as described beyond what is stated about DAST-20 in this study.

The packet supports DAST-20 as a drug-abuse screening tool and reports acceptable reliability/validity for the Tagalog version, but it does not explicitly support the claims that it is a questionnaire or that it gauges how severe a person’s drug use may be.
The packet does not support the description of DAST-20 as a “widely used 20-item version” in this wording; “20-item” is implied by the title, but “widely used” is not established in the packet text.
